sections.h2: What the Robertson County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
Title to Robertson County land moves through this office, which files warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, releases and plats. The Register holds an elected four year term. Doors are open weekdays from 8 to 4:30, and nothing is offered on weekends.

A home is usually the biggest purchase anyone makes, which is why accurate records matter here. For a seller, the deed is the paper that puts the new owner on the public record. Recording it is also what prompts the Assessor to update the parcel.

Staff can answer questions about fees, filing formats and what a document must contain. They cannot give legal advice or write an instrument for you, so a title company or lawyer remains the right source for the deed itself. If you are unsure which kind of deed fits your situation, settle that with your closing agent before you bring anything to the counter.

A warranty deed, quitclaim deed, deed of trust or lease is charged $5.00 for each page, with a $10.00 floor and a $2.00 electronic data processing fee on top. The Register's own $1.00 fee is added only on instruments that carry state tax.

Robertson County Register of Deeds recording fees
DocumentFee
Deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, agreements$5.00 per page, $10.00 minimum, plus $2.00 processing
Plat or survey map$15.00 per page plus $2.00 processing
Releases$10.00 for one or two pages and one lien, $5.00 per extra page or lien, plus $2.00
Assignments$10.00 for one or two pages, $5.00 per extra page or assignment, plus $2.00
Extra instrument in one document$5.00 each

An assignment must carry a statement of maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes.

sections.h2: What state tax applies to a Robertson County sale?
sections.html:
The state conveyance tax runs $3.70 on every $1,000 of value, the same as $0.37 per $100. The Register collects it under T.C.A. 67-4-409 at the time of recording. Add the $1.00 register's fee, plus the per-page charge and the $2.00 processing fee, and that is what a deed costs to record.

Loans are taxed separately at $1.15 per $1,000 of debt, with $2,000 left out of the calculation. That tax applies to the buyer's mortgage, not to the seller.

The statute exempts certain transfers, among them conveyances between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entirety, deeds that carry out a will, moves into and out of a revocable living trust, and divorce settlement deeds. A quitclaim is taxed only on the consideration actually paid. Your closing agent can tell you which treatment fits your deed. Ask for the exemption in writing if you think one applies, so the figure on the settlement statement matches what the Register collects.

sections.h2: How do I file or search records in Robertson County?
sections.html:
You may hand a paper original over the counter or send the file electronically. Online records begin January 1, 1998, and the office points researchers to ustitlesearch.com.

  • Electronic recording: accepted through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and ePN (eRecording Partners).
  • Paper filing: bring the original to the office during business hours along with payment.
  • Preparer details: state law requires a preparer's name and address on every document except releases and charters.
  • Drafting: a title company or lawyer should prepare the deed ahead of your visit.

For a full ownership history on an older parcel, a title company is the usual route. Online records cover only the years since the start date above, and anything earlier means asking staff or paying for a title search.

sections.h2: What the Assessor does after a deed is recorded
sections.html:
A copy of the recorded deed reaches the Assessor of Property the next day. Getting the buyer's name onto the parcel takes about 90 days, and in the meantime the next tax notice goes to whoever was on file for January 1.

Plan for that gap, because the current year's bill may still show your name after closing. The closing papers should spell out who pays for that year, and the address printed on the deed is what the Assessor uses for the following year's notice. The Assessor works at 521 S. Brown St. in Springfield, 615-384-4311. The Trustee, at 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, supplies tax payoffs.

sections.h2: How the Register, Assessor and Trustee fit together in a sale
sections.html:
A sale passes through three desks in a fixed order. The Register gets the deed, the Assessor sees it a day later, and the Trustee collects any tax still owing.

  • Before closing: call the Trustee for the balance on each parcel you own, because deeds are indexed under varied spellings and a name search alone can miss one.
  • At closing: state tax and recording charges are collected by the Register, and any open tax is settled with the Trustee.
  • After closing: the Assessor updates the owner name, and the address on the deed drives next year's bill.

A bill that reaches one year delinquent moves to Robertson County Chancery Court, 615-384-5650, and a suit is filed for the tax. Ask the Trustee which stage your bill is in before choosing a closing day.

For 2020 to 2024 the county counts 28,255 households averaging 2.65 people, and 89.8 percent of residents were at the same address a year before. Median monthly owner costs are $1,656 with a mortgage and $507 without one. Builders took out 823 permits in 2025. Springfield anchors the county, and Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier and Orlinda also record through the same Register.

The Register promotes My Land Alert, a service with free monitoring and notification, no contract and email privacy. Sign up at mylandalert.com to get a message when a document is recorded against your name.

Keep the recorded copy of your deed with your closing papers so you can match the instrument number the Register assigned. If an alert ever arrives for a document you do not recognize, call the office right away and bring that instrument number with you.

Recording goes fast when the paperwork is ready. Ahead of closing day, run down this list.

  1. Learn who is preparing the deed and whether it will be filed electronically or on paper.
  2. Confirm the preparer's name and address appear on the deed.
  3. Check that any lender being paid off has sent its release, so title reads clean.
  4. Get the Trustee's payoff for every parcel in your name.
  5. Keep the recorded copy afterward, with the instrument number the office assigns.

Even a cash buyer who takes the house as-is needs the deed recorded, so none of these steps drop away.

faqs.q: What is the minimum Robertson County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: $12.00 before tax: a $10.00 minimum charge plus the $2.00 processing fee. Longer deeds pay $5.00 per page, and a $1.00 register's fee is added when state tax is collected.

faqs.q: What is the Robertson County deed tax rate?
faqs.a: The state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value. Mortgages are taxed at $1.15 per $1,000 once the first $2,000 is set aside.

faqs.q: Does the Robertson County Register accept electronic filings?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners are listed. Paper originals are accepted at the counter during business hours.

faqs.q: How far back do Robertson County online deed records go?
faqs.a: Internet records begin January 1, 1998, searchable through ustitlesearch.com. For anything earlier, ask the Register's staff.

faqs.q: How long until a buyer appears on the Robertson County tax rolls?
faqs.a: About 90 days after the Assessor gets the recorded deed copy, which arrives the day after recording. The bill goes to the January 1 name until the next year.
